question: A simpler Notion
one_liner: A stripped-down Notion alternative for 5-20 person remote teams, priced per seat
verdict_sub: **The pain is real — but the people complaining aren't the buyers.**
verdict_sub2: "Notion is too complex" shows up across HN, App Store reviews and comparison blogs — but nearly every complaint traces to free individual users, while paying teams call the flexibility the reason they stay. Real demand exists one segment over: docs-first tools for non-technical small teams. Aim there, not at "simpler Notion."

claims.title: Pain exists: Notion overwhelms casual users
claims.note: Verified across 3 independent platforms — complexity complaints are loud and recurring.

claims.title: ICP match: small remote teams have this pain
claims.note: Complainers are free individual users; team admins praise the flexibility.

claims.title: They'd pay $15/seat for a simpler tool
claims.note: No payment evidence at that price; simpler rivals win on free tiers.

claims.title: Per-seat SaaS is the right model here
claims.note: Model works in the category, but only with a differentiated wedge.

go_criteria.criterion: ≥3 independent sources show the same willingness-to-pay signal
go_criteria.note: Only opinion-grade quotes found; zero payment behavior.

go_criteria.criterion: Complaint volume concentrated in the target ICP
go_criteria.note: Complaints skew to free individual users, not teams.

why.title: The complexity pain is real
why.body: "Too complex / gave up" recurs on HN, App Store (84,953 ratings) and comparison blogs — triangulated at 3 sources.

why.title: Buyer mismatch · lethal
why.body: Those who complain don't hold the budget; team admins who pay praise the flexibility that casual users hate.

why.title: No payment evidence at $15/seat
why.body: Every willingness-to-pay quote is opinion-grade; competitors compete on generous free tiers.

why.title: Red ocean, commoditized features
why.body: Slite, Craft, Coda and a dozen others already sell "simpler docs"; the feature set is table stakes.

why.title: A wedge exists one segment over
why.body: Non-technical teams (agencies, ops) want docs-first with zero database concepts — underserved per review mining.

one_thing.title: Pre-sell to non-technical teams before writing code
one_thing.detail: Run a landing-page pre-sale aimed at agencies/ops teams at $10/seat with $100 of ads; kill the idea if paid sign-ups stay under 2%.

actions.title: Re-target the ICP to non-technical small teams
actions.detail: Re-run validation on agencies/ops teams who never adopted Notion; 1 week of interview mining on their current stack.

actions.title: Test pricing against free tiers, not against Notion
actions.detail: Benchmark Slite/Craft free plans; find the jobs a free tier can't do and price only those. Decide in 1 week.

do_not.title: Don't build "simpler Notion" for Notion users
do_not.reason: The complaining segment doesn't pay; the paying segment doesn't want simpler.

do_not.title: Don't compete on feature count
do_not.reason: Docs features are commoditized across a dozen funded rivals.

risks.title: Free tiers cap the price ceiling
risks.body: Rivals' free plans cover the casual segment's whole job; paid conversion in this category runs low single digits, which can't fund paid acquisition.

risks.title: Notion's template ecosystem is the moat you'd fight
risks.body: Switching cost isn't features — it's thousands of community templates and integrations a newcomer can't match on day one.

voices.summary: Loud complexity complaints, but the same threads defend Notion's power for teams — the split maps exactly to free vs paying users.
1-2 star reviews repeat "overwhelming / too many concepts"; most are individual plans.
Collaboration-software market is growing, but no analyst sizes a "simpler docs" sub-segment.
"notion alternative simple" and "notion too complicated" both trend up year over year.

contradictions: Top-down and bottom-up agree the market is big and growing — but they split on *who* hurts: analysts talk team seats, while community complaints come from free individuals. That mismatch is the finding: the demand is real, the assumed buyer is wrong.
red_team: The lethal blow: **the complainers and the buyers are two different people.** Red team also killed the $15/seat claim (zero payment evidence, free-tier competition) — together these pulled the verdict from Conditional (55) to Pivot (40). It could NOT refute the pain itself, which survived at 3-source confidence.

alternatives.current: Notion with a strict "3 blocks only" team convention
alternatives.gap: Discipline decays; new hires break it — a tool-level constraint is the gap
No structure at all; teams outgrow it at ~10 people

not_verified: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE: every quote and URL here is a placeholder, nothing above was actually researched.
Market size for the "docs-first, non-technical teams" sub-segment — no analyst covers it (needs paid data).
Actual churn reasons of paying Notion teams — only anecdotes, no cohort data.
